What is a normative economic action based on?
Which function of money overcomes the double coincidence of wants problem that exists in a barter system?
The production possibility curves (PPCs) show the abilities of four economies to produce wheat and rice. Which PPC has the lowest opportunity cost for producing wheat? wheat (tonnes)
The diagram shows a supply curve for chicken. S price O quantity What explains why the supply curve for chicken slopes upwards?

options.A: An increase in the demand for chicken will bring about a rise in supply.
options.B: Farmers’ productivity rises as the price rises.
options.C: Increased production leads to a reduction in costs.
options.D: The cost of additional chicken production rises as output increases.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for cars in India. The initial equilibrium is at X. What will be the new equilibrium if there is a subsidy given to Indian car manufacturers and there is also an increase in the price of train and bus journeys in India? price S S
Demand curves are drawn ceteris paribus. Which ‘other things’ are not required to remain the same when an individual’s demand curve for ice cream is constructed?
What is the measure of cross-elasticity of demand for good X in terms of good Y?

options.A: the change in the demand for X divided by the change in the price of Y
options.B: the change in the price of X divided by the change in the demand for Y
options.C: the percentage change in the demand for X divided by the percentage change in the price of Y
options.D: the percentage change in the demand for Y divided by the percentage change in the price of X

questions.questionText: When will the price mechanism be least likely to reallocate resources to meet a change in consumer preferences?

options.A: when the government removes all price controls
options.B: when the new preferences are for more public goods
options.C: when the supply of factors of production is limited
options.D: when there is a redistribution of income

questions.questionText: A firm estimates that the price elasticity of supply of its product is +1.5. What does this indicate?

options.B: The firm has no excess capacity.
options.C: The firm operates in a competitive market.
options.D: The firm raises its price by 10% and its total revenue increases by 15%.

questions.questionText: A rise in the price of a good is accompanied by an increase in the quantity demanded. What could explain this?

options.A: Consumers spend a high proportion of disposable income on the good.
options.B: The price of a complementary good has also increased.
options.C: The price of the good is taken to be an indication of the level of quality.
options.D: The substitute goods are all very much more expensive.

questions.questionText: What causes the demand curve for an inferior good to shift to the right?

options.C: a decrease in the price of a substitute good
options.D: a decrease in the price of the good

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the effect of a change in the market for good X on the market for good Y. S price S price S

To improve its financial position, a government decided to reduce expenditure on investment in the public sector. There was not a fall in economic growth. What was the most likely effect of the government’s action?

options.A: An original budget deficit was reduced.
options.B: An original budget surplus was reduced.

questions.questionText: What are the effects of a government imposing a maximum price below the equilibrium price? demand supply
The National Library Board of Singapore is a public sector organisation that finances and manages the state libraries. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.C: The cost of providing library services would be greater in the private sector.
options.D: The opportunity cost to the public sector of providing library services is zero.

questions.questionText: Three types of tax are listed.  a sales tax (VAT) on fuel  a specific tax of 10% on cigarettes  the percentage of income tax on individual earnings increases as taxable income increases Which combination describes the effect of each of these types of tax? VAT specific tax income tax

The bus fare in a rural area is $5 per journey. The government decides to improve local transport by giving bus firms a subsidy of $2 per journey. The diagram shows the possible changes in demand and supply. S S S bus fare per journey ($) D D D quantity of journeys per week What is the new quantity of journeys and the bus fare for a journey? quantity of bus fare journeys ($)

The diagram shows the annual consumer prices index for Japan over the years 1990–2010 inclusive. consumer 4 prices 3 index (%) –1 –2 –3 1990 1992 1994 1996 1998 2000 2002 2004 2006 2008 2010 year In which period did Japan experience both inflation at a rate of approximately 2% and deflation at a rate of approximately 2.5%?
The terms of trade index for Mauritius fell from 111.2 in the first quarter of 2018 to 106.1 in the second quarter. Which combination could have produced this outcome? export prices import prices

From the initial position of equilibrium shown, there is an increase in government expenditure on goods and services and simultaneously an increase in the costs of production of goods and services. full employment price AS level AD O real output What best describes the likely impact on the economy? equilibrium level equilibrium level of national income of prices

Which item is not included in the current account on the balance of payments statement?

options.D: the interest received from investment overseas

questions.questionText: The prices of a country’s exports rise by 5% while the prices of its imports fall by 5%. What will definitely improve in the country as a result of these changes?
What is not a form of protectionism?

Two countries, X and Y, produce food and drink. The table shows how many hours it takes them to produce one unit of each. food drink X 10 2 Y 20 12 What will be the result if country Y doubles its productivity in the output of drink and both countries produce only one good according to comparative advantage?

options.A: X will continue to produce drink.
options.B: Y will produce drink instead of food.

questions.questionText: ‘Reducing the exchange rate helps to decrease a country’s balance of payments deficit because it makes imports more expensive and exports cheaper.’ What does this statement describe?
An increase in which variable is a contractionary monetary policy?
What are government monetary policies that would be the most effective in a global recession?

options.A: allowing the rate of interest to fluctuate and increasing business taxation
options.B: increasing the budget surplus and raising tariffs on imports
options.C: keeping the rate of interest very low and increasing the money supply
